The loss function is the weighted mean squared error between the predicted noise and the actual noise [S1]:

The evidence explicitly states the loss function formula in Source [S1] as L = E_{t~U(0,T), ϵ~N(0,I)} [γ(t) ||ϵ_ϕ(z_t, y, t) - ϵ||^2_2]. The term ||ϵ_ϕ(z_t, y, t) - ϵ||^2_2 represents the squared L2 norm (squared error) between the predicted noise (ϵ_ϕ) and the actual noise (ϵ). The term γ(t) acts as a weight for each timestep. Since the expectation is taken over the distribution of timesteps and noise samples, this constitutes a weighted mean squared error. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
